title: Local Zero Branches and Degenerate Splitting in a Multiplicative Residual Operator
content: The local behavior of the zeros of the multiplicative residual operator \( \Delta_q F(x)=qF(qx)-F(q^2x) \) is studied in the limit \( q\to1 \). Since \( \Delta_1F(x)=0 \) identically, a zero at \( q=1 \) does not by itself determine the behavior of the zero set for nearby values of the parameter. Expanding the operator around \( q=1 \) leads to the reduced condition \( F(x_*)-x_*F'(x_*)=0. \) For a regular zero satisfying \( x_*>0 \) and \( F''(x_*)\neq0 \), the reduced equation admits a unique local continuation, and the corresponding zero of the original operator has the expansion \( x(q)=x_*-\frac{3}{2}x_*(q-1)+O\left((q-1)^2\right). \) The coefficient of the first-order displacement is independent of the particular function \( F \). The degenerate case \( F''(x_*)=0 \) is treated separately, since the regular implicit-function argument no longer applies. An explicit example is examined in which the leading higher-order equation produces complex conjugate coefficients rather than a real branch of the assumed form. Numerical calculations for a regular example provide a stringent consistency check of the local expansion, with computed residuals of order \( 10^{-102} \)—\( 10^{-101} \) in the reported calculations. A homogeneous family is also considered to distinguish pointwise zeros from exact kernel identities, with the linear relation \( F(k)=ck \) selected by the corresponding exact condition. The results are local and do not constitute a classification of the global zero set or of higher-order degeneracies.
